rules: content_type describes what a record is; primary_loc describes who owns its canonical definition.
A media representation of a LOC3/LOC4 work receives its own LOC5 media_id and references the source work_id.
Unified search may filter by content_type without exposing LOC numbers to the user.
README.md and other overview documents may be indexed as knowledge_document while preserving their derived/provenance status.
display_policy governs public text exposure independently from whether full text may be indexed or analyzed internally.
Author-created Facebook/Threads raw text is LOC4 life-writing content; LOC6 may consume the same records for governance/style interpretation without taking ownership of the raw text.
LOC4/LOC6 boundary: raw authored text, including Facebook/Threads life writing, is LOC4; governance/value/Zhengde-style interpretation derived from it is LOC6.
A quoted source statement inside a LOC6 governance record is evidence, not transfer of ownership of the original text.
General literary/semantic work analysis is LOC4. Only governance/style/value interpretation of that material is LOC6.
Public category and source platform are separate dimensions: authored text defaults to public_category=文字創作 regardless of platform.
content_type may preserve subtype such as novel, article, essay, journal, social_text_record, or text_record without changing the public category.
source_platform records provenance such as Threads, Facebook, Instagram, X(Twitter), Vocus, or another actual source; source platform must not replace the public category.
X(Twitter) may be configured as a source label/test source without ingesting private or non-public posts.

display_policy.enforcement: Apply only at public response/export boundary. Full text may remain available internally for authorized indexing, analysis, Graph and RAG.
notes: snippet returns only a query-relevant preview and must not expose full text through payload fields.
full allows full public text only when rights/visibility governance also permits it.
metadata_only returns bibliographic/source metadata without body text.
